lessons.title: Non-Fiction: Who Was Wassily Kandinsky?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about Kandinsky's life from a non-fiction text.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about Kandinsky.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a Kandinsky painting and discuss initial reactions.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a non-fiction text about Kandinsky's life and style.
lessons.independent_task: Children read an extract and answer retrieval questions.
key_questions: Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Look up a Kandinsky painting together.

lessons.title: Shapes and Circles in Kandinsky's Art
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify and describe circles and other shapes within Kandinsky's artwork.
success_criteria: I can name shapes in the artwork.
I can describe their size and position.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model identifying and describing circles and other shapes in Kandinsky's artwork, including concentric circles.
lessons.independent_task: Children identify and describe shapes in a Kandinsky artwork, focusing on size and position.
key_questions: Are any circles inside each other?

differentiation.greater_depth: Describe multiple shapes and their relative positions

lessons.assessment_notes: Note shape recognition applied to an art analysis context, including the new term 'concentric' — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.plenary: Recap shapes identified in the artwork.
lessons.home_link: Look for circles within circles at home.

lessons.title: Studying Kandinsky's Abstract Style
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe features of Kandinsky's abstract style.
success_criteria: I can describe what I notice in a Kandinsky painting.
I can say it doesn't show real objects.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a Kandinsky abstract painting.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss features of abstract art — using shape and colour rather than showing real objects.
lessons.independent_task: Children describe what they notice in a Kandinsky painting, recording their observations.
key_questions: What do you notice about this painting?
Does it show a real object?

differentiation.support: Point to and describe one feature
differentiation.greater_depth: Describe multiple features and give an opinion

lessons.assessment_notes: Note observational and descriptive skill studying an artist, extending understanding of abstract art — evidence for ART.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap features of abstract art discussed.
lessons.home_link: Look at more Kandinsky paintings together if possible.

lessons.title: Writing About a Kandinsky Painting
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write sentences describing what they see and feel in a Kandinsky painting.
success_criteria: I can write what I see.
I can write how it makes me feel.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing descriptive sentences about a Kandinsky painting, including how it makes you feel.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 sentences describing a Kandinsky artwork and their feelings about it.
key_questions: What can you see in the painting?
How does it make you feel?

differentiation.greater_depth: Write 4+ sentences with detailed description and feeling

lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive writing about visual art including personal response — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share painting descriptions with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Describe how a picture makes you feel at home.

lessons.title: Counting Circles: Kandinsky Style
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count and represent numbers using a Kandinsky-inspired circles context.
success_criteria: I can count circles in a set.
I can represent the number using tens and ones.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model counting sets of circle counters (inspired by Kandinsky), representing with tens and ones.
lessons.independent_task: Children count and represent circle counter quantities using base-10 blocks.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record place value consolidation applied to an art-themed context — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.home_link: Count circles you can find at home.

lessons.title: Creating Concentric Circle Art
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to create artwork using concentric circles in the style of Kandinsky.
success_criteria: I can paint circles within circles.
I can use different colours purposefully.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model painting concentric circles using different colours, in the style of Kandinsky.
lessons.independent_task: Children create their own concentric circle artwork.
key_questions: What colours will you use for each circle?
How many circles will you paint?

differentiation.greater_depth: Paint freehand circles with a wider colour range

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe application of a specific artist's technique — evidence for ART.1/ART.2.
lessons.home_link: Look for circles within circles in objects at home.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Colour and Shape Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read colour/shape-themed words.
success_criteria: I can read colour and shape words.
I can read a sentence about art.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to colour/shape-themed words (e.g. 'circle', 'yellow', 'bright').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading colour and shape words over the week.

lessons.title: Kandinsky-Themed Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction word problems using an art context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap addition and subtraction strategies to 100.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems using an art context (e.g. circles painted in different colours).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve art-themed word problems within 100, showing working.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up an art-themed word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Kandinsky-Inspired Music and Colour
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to represent music/sound using colour and shape, inspired by Kandinsky's synaesthesia-influenced work.
success_criteria: I can choose colours to represent a sound.
I can explain my choices.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss that Kandinsky said he could 'see' music as colour.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model listening to a piece of music and choosing colours/shapes to represent how it sounds/feels.
lessons.independent_task: Children listen to a short piece of music and create an artwork representing it using colour and shape.
key_questions: What colours does this music make you think of?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain reasoning for choices in detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe creative interpretation and application of Kandinsky's approach — evidence for ART.1/ART.2.
lessons.plenary: Share music-inspired artworks and guess which music inspired which piece.
lessons.home_link: Listen to music and think about what colours it makes you imagine.

lessons.title: Presenting Our Kandinsky-Inspired Art
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to present their Kandinsky-inspired artwork and explain their choices.
success_criteria: I can describe my artwork.
I can explain my colour/shape choices.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap Kandinsky's style studied this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what makes a clear presentation about artwork and creative choices.
lessons.independent_task: Children present their concentric circle or music-inspired artwork to a small group.
key_questions: Why did you choose these colours/shapes?

differentiation.greater_depth: Present unprompted with confidence and detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and art reflection progress — evidence for ENG.SL1/ART.2.
lessons.home_link: Present your artwork to your family.

lessons.title: Fractions: Colour Proportions in Kandinsky's Art
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply fraction knowledge to describe colour proportions in an artwork.
success_criteria: I can estimate a fraction of colour used.
I can use fraction language.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model using fraction language to estimate colour proportions in a Kandinsky painting.
lessons.independent_task: Children estimate and record fractions of colour used in their own or Kandinsky's artwork.
key_questions: What fraction of the painting is this colour?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of fractions to a creative/visual context, consolidating the term — evidence for MATHS.N4.
lessons.home_link: Estimate a fraction of colour in a picture at home.

lessons.title: Comparing Picasso and Kandinsky
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare the styles of Picasso and Kandinsky.
success_criteria: I can name a similarity.
I can name a difference.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap both artists studied over the two weeks.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing Picasso's cubism to Kandinsky's abstract style.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare the two artists, recording similarities and differences.
key_questions: What is similar about these styles?

differentiation.support: Compare with adult support, one similarity/difference

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparative art analysis skill across two studied artists — evidence for ART.2.
lessons.home_link: Discuss which artist's style your family prefers and why.

lessons.title: Wassily Kandinsky Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about Wassily Kandinsky.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's learning about Kandinsky.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about Kandinsky, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: Why might he have linked music to colour?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on Kandinsky facts you learned.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Shape, Number, Fractions
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply shape, number and fraction skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can name shapes.
I can represent numbers with tens and ones.
I can estimate fractions.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of shape, number, and fractions.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations covering each skill.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 30 maths observations for each child, completing Summer 1 — evidence for MATHS.GEO/N1/N4.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising fractions over the weekend.

lessons.title: Picasso and Kandinsky Unit Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about both artists studied.
success_criteria: I can describe both artists' styles.
I can say which I prefer and why.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the two weeks' learning about Picasso and Kandinsky.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a final review and contribute to a class 'Artists We've Studied' display featuring both weeks' art.
key_questions: What have we learned about these two artists?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: End of two-week artist study consolidation summary for each child — evidence for ART.2.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate a fantastic two weeks of artist study, completing Summer 1.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about Picasso and Kandinsky with your family.
